question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\text{E}[{X}^{2}+3X].$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.7$ | $0.2$ |
question.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\sum }_{x\in S}r(x)f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={x}^{2}+3x.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+3X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}({x}^{2}+3x)\,f(x) \\  & =({1}^{2}+3\cdot 1)\cdot 0.1+({2}^{2}+3\cdot 2)\cdot 0.7+({3}^{2}+3\cdot 3)\cdot 0.2 \\  & =4\cdot 0.1+10\cdot 0.7+18\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.4+7+3.6 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$
